exposure.statement: Acute reference point (lowest BMDL10) for hypersensitivity (eczema flare-up) in nickel-sensitised individuals.

In 'Other children' and 'Adolescents' the relatively high consumption of chocolate and chocolate-based products made 'Sugar and confectionery' one of the main contributors; cocoa beverages explain the important role of non-alcoholic beverages in the young.

Other children: Sugar and confectionery median 10.7% of Ni exposure (>10% in eight surveys), driven by chocolate-based products; non-alcoholic beverages (3.0-39.3%, median 14.4%) driven by cocoa beverages.
Adolescents: non-alcoholic beverages 6.4-36.0% (median 16.6%) and sugar and confectionery 4.4-22.0% (median 10.6%), mainly due to cocoa beverages and chocolate-based products.
Toddlers/infants: sugar and confectionery peaked at 16.9% and 19.8% in two surveys; non-alcoholic beverages 41.8% in one survey due to high consumption of cocoa beverages.
Elderly and very elderly: lower chocolate consumption; sugar and confectionery median 3.8% and 4.7%.
Mean chronic dietary Ni exposure ranged 2.0 (min LB, elderly) to 13.1 (max UB, toddlers) µg/kg bw/day; P95 3.6-20.1.
Dilution factor 60 used to convert cocoa powder to cocoa beverage for exposure.
